tail:
1. **Fatal — `ex-free-group-on-the-empty-set` — title, Example, proof step 2.1, and proof contract.**  
   The proof establishes only that the particular quotient model \(F_{\mathrm{word}}(\varnothing)\) has one element. It never transfers this conclusion to an arbitrary free group on \(\varnothing\). The published definition characterizes free groups by the universal property, while `thm-word-quotient-model-is-free` establishes that the quotient model is **a** free group. The necessary transfer is supplied by `thm-free-groups-unique-up-to-unique-isomorphism`, whose Statement says that any two free groups on \(X\) are uniquely generator-compatible isomorphic. That theorem is absent from `deps`, Facts, and step 2.1. The contract likewise lists only step 1.1 as input to step 2.1. Thus [the title and line 27](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/ex-free-group-on-the-empty-set.md:4) assert “the free group” where the proof handles only one model—the precise run-specific fatal pattern.

2. **Fatal — `ex-free-group-on-one-generator` — title, Example, proof step 3.1, and proof contract.**  
   Step 3.1 correctly proves
   \[
   F_{\mathrm{word}}(\{x\})\cong\mathbb Z
   \]
   using normal forms and cyclic-group classification. It does not prove the title’s claim about **the** free group on one generator. Again, `thm-free-groups-unique-up-to-unique-isomorphism` is absent from `deps` and Facts. Its generator-compatible isomorphism is exactly what is needed to transport the result from the quotient model to every free group on \(\{x\}\). The contract records only `[L2]` and step 2.1 as inputs to step 3.1. Compare [the title and Example](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/ex-free-group-on-one-generator.md:4) with step 3.1.

3. **Fatal — `ex-presentation-of-z-squared` — Example Statement, line 29.**  
   The displayed presentation isomorphism \(P\cong\mathbb Z^2\) is proved correctly: every element has form \(a^mb^n\), and the coordinate map has trivial kernel. But the preceding sentence claims that this is “the free abelian group on two generators.” The local [definition of a free abelian group](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-free-abelian-group.md:25) requires an extension-and-uniqueness property for every map into every abelian group. No step proves or cites that universal property, and neither `def-free-abelian-group` nor an equivalent theorem is a dependency. The proof contract also contains only the \(P\cong\mathbb Z^2\) argument. Thus [the Example Statement](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/ex-presentation-of-z-squared.md:29) asserts strictly more than the proof supplies.

4. **Fatal — `ex-presentation-of-a-dihedral-group` — title, Example lines 29–32, proof steps 1.3, 2.1, and 4.1.**  
   The proof validly establishes
   \[
   P\cong\langle\rho,\sigma\rangle\leq\operatorname{Sym}(\mathbb Z/n):
   \]
   it proves the \(2n\) permutation normal forms are distinct, gives the von Dyck surjection, and proves the matching \(2n\)-form upper bound in \(P\). It does **not** establish that \(\langle\rho,\sigma\rangle\) is the full symmetry group of a regular \(n\)-gon. Step 1.3 simply rewrites the target as \(D_n=\langle\rho,\sigma\rangle\), and step 2.1 calls surjectivity onto \(D_n\) true “by definition,” although the Example first defines \(D_n\) as the full polygon symmetry group and asserts generation as a claim. The Given mentions only \(n,\mathbb Z/n,\rho,\sigma\).

   The published `ex-symmetries-of-a-square` avoids this issue by defining a vertex symmetry through preservation of the edge relation and then proving that every such symmetry lies in the generated subgroup. No analogous definition or exhaustion argument appears here. Accordingly, [the title’s named target](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/ex-presentation-of-a-dihedral-group.md:4) is stronger than what is proved. I classify this fatal under the run’s title/Statement rule. My only uncertainty is whether the opening prose was intended stipulatively as \(D_n:=\langle\rho,\sigma\rangle\); that is not what its current wording says.

## 2. Items read and accepted

- `ex-free-group-on-two-generators-is-not-abelian` — checked distinct reduced words \(xy\) and \(yx\), normal-form uniqueness, and transfer through the generator-compatible unique isomorphism.
- `ex-presentation-of-a-finite-cyclic-group` — checked negative exponents, the \(n\)-normal-form upper bound, distinct/exhaustive target images, and \(n=1\).
- `ex-presentation-of-the-klein-four-group` — checked the four normal forms and their four distinct images.
- `ex-presentation-of-the-symmetric-group-on-three-letters` — recomputed the six permutation images under rightmost-first composition and verified the alternating-word shortening gives at most six forms.
- `cex-delete-only-relator-rewriting-misses-ba` — recomputed \(ab=e\Rightarrow b=a^{-1}\Rightarrow ba=e\); `ba` contains neither a free cancellation nor `ab` nor \(b^{-1}a^{-1}\).
- `cex-delete-only-relator-rewriting-can-require-lengthening` — recomputed triviality using \(ab=ba\); checked all five length-four windows of `aabbAABB`, its absence of adjacent inverse pairs, and both relator orientations.
- `cex-delete-only-relator-rewriting-is-order-dependent` — recomputed triviality of the presented group and both terminal paths \(\varepsilon\) and `a`.

The van der Waerden dependency spine also passed: \(\lambda_a\) lands in reduced words in both cases, both composition orders with \(\lambda_{a^{-1}}\) are verified, and normal-form uniqueness is obtained by evaluating the induced permutation at \(\varepsilon\), without circularly assuming uniqueness.

No assigned item makes a computability or decidability claim. All direct dependency targets have eligible `literature-derived` or `ai-altered` statement provenance; none is `ai-generated`.

## 3. Anything not verified

All local dependency Definitions and Statements were located and read. I could not inspect the externally linked Minasyan PDF from the checkout because no local copy is present; none of the findings above relies on its contents.
